easy.def: The place where an animal or plant lives.
examples: A pond is a frog's habitat.
The sea is a whale's habitat.
A bird's habitat can be a forest.

more.def: The natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds what it needs to live.
examples: The desert is the habitat of many lizards and snakes.
When forests are cut down, animals lose their habitat.
The zoo built a habitat that looks like a snowy mountain.

easy.def: The part at the end of your arm.
examples: Wash your hands.
I raise my hand.
She held my hand.

more.def: The part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers and a thumb that is used for holding things.
examples: He held a small frog in his hand.
Raise your hand if you know the answer.
The clock has two hands, one for hours and one for minutes.
Hand me the cup.
She handed me a pencil.
Please hand it over.

more.def: To give something to someone by passing it straight to them.
examples: Please hand the scissors to your sister.
The teacher handed out a worksheet to each student.
He handed her the umbrella as she left.
What will happen next?
It happened last night.
Rainbows happen after rain.

more.def: To take place, often without being planned.
examples: A strange thing happened on the way to school today.
Do you know what happens to ice when it gets warm?
The accident happened so quickly that nobody saw it.

easy.def: A safe place by the land for boats.
examples: The boats are in the harbor.
We saw big ships in the harbor.
A seal swam in the harbor.

more.def: A sheltered area of water where ships can stay safely.
examples: Fishing boats returned to the harbor before the storm.
The city grew up around its busy harbor.
Sailboats bobbed gently in the harbor.

easy.def: To pick food that has grown.
examples: We harvest corn from the field.
We harvest pumpkins in the fall.
The farmer harvests the wheat.

more.def: To gather crops when they are ripe and ready.
examples: Farmers harvest apples in the fall.
We harvested tomatoes from our garden all summer.
Workers harvest the grapes by hand.
I have a red ball.
She has two cats.
We had a nice time.

more.def: To own something, to hold it, or to be given or filled with something.
examples: My cousin has a telescope for looking at the stars.
Spiders have eight legs.
We had pancakes for breakfast on Saturday.
